segments.text: The README sets a challenge: push a file called key dot txt, containing the phrase May I come in, to the master branch.
I log in as bandit31 with ssh bandit31@bandit.labs.overthewire.org -p 2220.
The lab blocks the localhost ssh hop, so I clone from this client.
I read the README and the gitignore: the file must be key dot txt, with the content May I come in, on branch master, and the gitignore excludes all dot txt files.
I write the file with echo.
A normal git add would quietly ignore it, so I use git add minus f, which overrides the ignore rule.
The commit records one file changed, one insertion.
Then I push to origin master.
The push sends the objects, and the remote hook validates the file, prints Well done, and gives the password for bandit thirty-two.
The hook declines the push, so git reports the push failed, but the remote output already gave the password for bandit thirty-two, and the level is solved.
